data.title: Middle East Eye: UKMTO says 11 ships attacked in week to 4 Nov in Hormuz, Arabian Gulf
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
UKMTO says 11 ships attacked in week to 4 Nov in Hormuz, Arabian Gulf
The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) has reported 11 attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and Arabian Gulf in the seven days to November 4, including incidents that left three vessels sunk.
Eight attacks occurred in the Strait of Hormuz and three in the Arabian Gulf, according to UKMTO's weekly overview. Of the 11 incidents, three vessels continued their voyages, five required assistance and three sank.
The report said one dhow was struck by an unidentified projectile on 2 November, killing one crew member, while 13 others were rescued by local authorities.
A Panama-flagged supply vessel was also struck by an unidentified projectile in the Strait of Hormuz on 1 November and reportedly sank after a nearby merchant vessel rescued its crew.
A Marshall Islands-flagged tanker was struck by two unidentified projectiles in the Arabian Gulf on 4 November, leaving it drifting and requiring assistance from local authorities.
Combined Strait of Hormuz traffic reached 325 transits in the seven-day reporting period, comprising 170 outbound and 155 inbound movements, compared with 277 in the previous week. UKMTO said traffic remained approximately 65 percent below pre-conflict levels.
Automatic Identification System-observed transits increased to 71 from 64 the previous week, while US-reported facilitated transits remained broadly stable. Around 80 percent of Strait of Hormuz transits continued to involve energy carriers.
UKMTO also reported an increase in vessels using the southern route, although most ships broadcasting AIS continued to use the Iranian route.
In the Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb, no attacks on shipping were reported during the week. The last reported attack was on August 24, 65 days earlier. However, Bab el-Mandeb transits remained 24 percent below levels recorded before the Houthi blockade announcement on July 22.

data.title: Middle East Eye: US offers $20 million reward for info on Iran's nuclear programme
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
US offers $20 million reward for info on Iran's nuclear programme
Washington is offering a $20 million reward "and possible relocation" for information about Iran's nuclear programme, the US military said Friday, as President Donald Trump reiterated Tehran wants to make a deal to end the war.
A State Department programme, Rewards for Justice, "is offering a reward of up to $20 million and possible relocation for information about Iran's nuclear program, including its facilities, equipment, and associated personnel, such as those in the scientific community," US Central Command said on X.
The programme was established in 1984 under the State Department's national security rewards programme to offer money for information that protects American lives and interests.
In its statement about the reward, the State Department said Iran's "lack of compliance with the IAEA (International Atomic Energy Agency) on safeguards obligations" has led to the agency's loss of 'continuity of knowledge' regarding Iran's production and inventory of key components like centrifuges.
It gave no specific parameters on what information would yield a $20 million reward.

data.title: Middle East Eye: 'Crisis cannot be left unresolved': Qatar PM says mediation efforts continue
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
'Crisis cannot be left unresolved': Qatar PM says mediation efforts continue
Qatar’s Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani, has said that efforts at mediation between Iran and the United States remain active to prevent escalation, warning that the crisis "cannot be left unresolved".
During a public interview at Oxford University on Friday, Al Thani said that “for the past couple of weeks, we have worked with colleagues in the US administration who have very genuine intentions to find a way to contain the situation and de-escalate it".
He said that mediation efforts continue “to prevent the situation from spiralling out of control,” adding that “thanks also to some wise voices in Tehran, we have prevented that from getting out of control.”
The prime minister also stressed that “we will never have a perfect peace deal, but we cannot just wait for this moment of a perfect deal and avoid having a good deal”.
He said that even after the US midterm election, the "intentions are still there, the willingness to take steps toward finding a solution is still there and we are building and capitalising on this".
Al Thani said that "our engagement did not stop and will not stop", although the current pace of diplomatic exchanges may not "be as active as it was a few days ago”.
Qatar earlier dismissed reports claiming negotiations between the US and Iran have failed, warning that such claims benefit “only those seeking to prolong the war”.
Al Thani said mediation efforts continue to prevent a major escalation. (AFP)

data.title: Middle East Eye: Trump says US knocked out Iranian 'little bit of anti-aircraft device'
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Trump says US knocked out Iranian 'little bit of anti-aircraft device'
US President Donald Trump says Washington had made considerable progress in its dealings with Iran, while acknowledging that US forces had carried out limited strikes against targets on the country.
"I don't want to talk about it. We do minor strikes. But they knocked out... and they built a little bit of an anti-aircraft device. And we knocked it out in about 15 minutes, maybe five," Trump told reporters when asked about reports of strikes near Iran's Qeshm Island.
Speaking to reporters after arriving aboard Air Force One at Donald J. Trump International Airport, Trump said the United States was taking out more Iranian oil than before the conflict.
"We've made a lot of progress with Iran, we're taking out more oil now than we were before the war. It's not a war," he said.
"You know, in Russia-Ukraine, they lose 25,000 people a month. We haven't lost anybody in seven months, so I don't think that's a war. Total control. But we're dealing with the Iranians, we'll see how that all works out."

Iranian forces on higher alert, stronger than before war, spokesman says
Iran's military is "stronger" and more motivated than it was when the United States and Israel started the war in February, says Iranian army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia.
"Today, the Islamic Republic's armed forces... having gained experience from direct confrontation with the United States and the Israeli regime, are on higher alert and are stronger than they were at the beginning of the war," Akraminia said, according to the state news agency Irna.
"They now possess greater motivation, commitment, and self-confidence."
Akraminia said that Iranian armed forces retained control over the Strait of Hormuz and that it would remain closed until the United States accepted Tehran's demands.
"Under the order of the Supreme Leader, the response of the armed forces will be immediate, effective, and without geographical limitations," he added.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Israeli settler attacks on West Bank olive harvest hit record since 2006, UN says
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Israeli settler attacks on West Bank olive harvest hit record since 2006, UN says
The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) has said Israeli settlers have carried out a total of 377 attacks on olive harvest across the occupied West Bank since September, a record since 2006 when the UN began recording them.
In a statement, OCHA said that during these attacks, one Palestinian was killed by a settler, more than 200 Palestinians were injured, and over 3,850 olive trees and saplings were damaged or vandalised.
Combined with official Israeli restrictions on Palestinian access to groves, this has undermined the livelihoods of many by reducing the produce that Palestinians could collect, the statement read.
Food security partners estimate that 80,000 to 100,000 Palestinian families across the West Bank depend on the annual olive harvest for their livelihoods and income.
* Gaza : OCHA said restrictions continue to hamper aid to Gaza despite widespread humanitarian response.
Humanitarian partners warn that the entry of engine oil, spare parts, generators, heavy machinery and specialised equipment remain particularly restricted. This prevents the implementation of more sustainable shelter solutions and risks shutting down critical services if back-up generators fail, according to the statement.
The attacks have resulted in the death of a Palestinian and injury to 200 others. (AFP)

data.title: Middle East Eye: 'It would facilitate Gaza genocide': Protesters storm Microsoft planned site
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
'It would facilitate Gaza genocide': Protesters storm Microsoft planned site
Several hundred activists occupied the construction site of a planned Microsoft data centre in Amsterdam on Friday, protesting the technology giant's alleged role in facilitating Israel's genocide in Gaza, as well as the environmental impact of artificial intelligence infrastructure.
The demonstration, organised by climate and justice collective Geef Tegengas and environmental group Fossielvrij, halted construction work for the day in the city's Sloterdijk district.
The protesters argued that the facility could be used to support AI-powered warfare and Israel's military operations in Gaza.
"It's so many things, so many struggles that come together in this data centre," Nathan Timmer, a spokesman for Geef Tegengas, told AFP.
Timmer, 30, accused the project of helping to facilitate "AI warfare" and what he described as the "genocide" in Gaza.
Dutch news agency ANP reported that police arrested between 150 and 200 protesters, while others left voluntarily.
The protest was part of a wider two-day mobilisation across Europe called by the Stop Dirty Data Centers coalition, which is demanding a pause in the construction of new data centre facilities.
Report by AFP

data.title: Middle East Eye: US-Israeli former soldier on visit to Netherlands accused of Gaza war crimes
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
US-Israeli former soldier on visit to Netherlands accused of Gaza war crimes
The Hind Rajab Foundation (HRF) has filed a criminal complaint in the Netherlands against a former US-Israeli soldier accused of involvement in attacks on schools sheltering displaced Palestinians, mass detentions and the destruction of residential buildings in Gaza.
The complaint, submitted to the Dutch National Public Prosecutor's Office on 4 November, names Noam Himmelman, a former member of the Israeli army's Netzah Yehuda Battalion, who is currently in Amsterdam.
HRF alleges that Himmelman was involved in war crimes, crimes against humanity and acts of genocide during Israel's war on Gaza. The complaint was filed under the Dutch International Crimes Act, which allows prosecution of international crimes when suspects are present on Dutch territory.
According to HRF, Israeli forces, including the battalion, surrounded schools in Beit Hanoun on 16 April 2024, where thousands of displaced Palestinians had sought shelter. Soldiers allegedly fired on the school complex and detained dozens of men, including elderly people and teenagers, forcing them to strip before taking them away.
HRF says Himmelman documented the arrests in an Instagram story that it subsequently verified and geolocated to a military outpost near the school.
The foundation also alleges that between January and July 2025, the battalion conducted controlled demolitions of residential buildings across Beit Hanoun, contributing to the extensive destruction of the town. Himmelman served with the unit during these operations.
The complaint cites the battalion's previous record of alleged abuses, including the 2022 death of 78-year-old Palestinian-American Omar Assad after he was detained by its soldiers.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Trump claims 'minor strikes' on Iran's Qeshm Island, but says talks ongoing
data.author: MEE staff
data.summary:
Trump claims 'minor strikes' on Iran's Qeshm Island, but says talks ongoing
Submitted by
MEE staff
on
Sat, 11/07/2026 - 09:13
The claimed attack comes shortly after Trump's Republican Party suffered a crushing defeat in the US midterm elections
US President Donald Trump speaks during NASA's Max Power event at the Kennedy Space Center, in Merritt Island, Florida, US, November 6, 202 (REUTERS)
Off
US President Donald Trump said on Friday that the American military carried out a new round of "minor strikes" on Iran's Qeshm Island, which he claimed "knocked out" Iranian air defence systems.
Iranian state media reported that two blasts were heard in the Suza area of Qeshm Island, which lies in the Strait of Hormuz, the contested waterway which has been disrupted since the US launched its assault on Iran in February.
The Iranian army said in comments carried by state broadcaster IRIB that their air defences downed a US drone over the island.
But Trump told reporters shortly after that the attacks "knocked out" the air defence systems "in about 15 minutes, maybe five".
Responding to reports of the explosions, US Central Command (Centcom) said that the situation is "relatively calm".
In a post on X late on Friday, it said that the US is “offering a reward of up to $20 million and possible relocation for information about Iran’s nuclear program, including its facilities, equipment, and associated personnel, such as those in the scientific community, or the movement of any of the above”.
This comes after the US military reported that it had conducted what it described as "defensive strikes" on Monday.
The latest round of strikes is the first since Trump's Republican Party suffered a crushing defeat in the US midterm elections- a loss which was fuelled in part by Trump's war on Iran and subsequent rocketing of energy prices.
Since then, Trump's messaging has been erratic- oscillating between threats to "destroy" Iran and claims that the war is close to being concluded.

Houthi media says 11 killed in Saudi strikes on Yemen's Sanaa province
Houthi media said on Saturday that Saudi strikes killed 11 people, including women and children, in Yemen's Sanaa province, following the return of the country's dormant civil war.
"Martyrdom of 11 citizens, among them women and children, in Saudi enemy airstrikes" on homes in the Al-Shariyah area of Sanaa province, the Iran-backed Houthis' Saba news agency said, adding that operations to recover victims from the rubble were ongoing and that "aircraft targeted paramedics with two strikes".

data.title: Middle East Eye: Rains flood Gaza displacement camps as Israeli authorities block entry of shelter materials into territory
data.author: Katherine Hearst
data.summary:
Rains flood Gaza displacement camps as Israeli authorities block entry of shelter materials into territory
Thousands of tents sheltering displaced Palestinians have been flooded by heavy rains overnight, exacerbating an already dire humanitarian situation.
Scarce aid entering the territory has left tens of thousands of Palestinians in the war-torn enclave exposed to the elements for a fourth winter in a row- with no fuel and nothing but makeshift tents and shelters for protection.
Red Cross spokesperon Amani Al Naouq told Al Jazeera that she has seen footage of “entire families, entire camps” inundated with water and scrambling to drain their tents and protect their belongings and lives.
In October, Director General for the International Organization for Migration Amy Pope warned that nearly all of Gaza's population require shelter assistance, with the combined supply pipeline of humanitarian shelter partners covering barely 17 per cent of identified winter needs.
"Families who have already endured repeated displacement and devastating loss must be able to face the winter in safety and dignity," Pope said. "Shelter materials must enter quickly, predictably and at the scale required."
Israel has continued to tightly restrict the entry of aid into the territory, with shelter items- including tent poles, construction materials and mobile homes- almost completely barred as the Israeli authorities consider them "dual use" items.
IOM said that around 8,600 IOM emergency shelter kits are waiting outside Gaza, but continue to be turned away from crossing points by the Israeli authorities.
This has forced humanitarian workers to repurpose salvaged materials to construct makeshift shelters, as storms turbochared by the strengthening El Niño phenomenon batter the territory.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Yemeni government forces claim attack on Houthi positions in al-Misrakh, while Saudi attacks on Bani Hashih kill at least 15
data.author: Katherine Hearst
data.summary:
Yemeni government forces claim attack on Houthi positions in al-Misrakh, while Saudi attacks on Bani Hashih kill at least 15
Yemeni government forces have claimed three air attacks on Houthi positions in the al-Misrakh district of the Taiz governorate.
The city of Taiz- which is government-held- has been subject to an ongoing Houthi siege. The blockade has triggered a spiralling humanitarian crisis in the city, as road closures bar vital supplies, including fuel, from entering.
Laurent Bukera, the United Nations Humanitarian Coordinator for Yemen warned that the city's health system is "close to collapse", while the UN World Food Programme (WFP) said that the conflict has blocked lifesaving assistance from reaching 800,000 people, including 600,000 who depend on aid in the city.
Meanwhile, Houthi media reports that at least 15 people have been killed, mostly women and children, in a series of Saudi strikes in the al-Shariyah area of Yemen’s Bani Hashish district. According to the reports, some 30 others have been wounded.
